paragraphs: **Thesis.** A dollar- and price-risk-neutral US equity long/short book. It blends {a:adm.n_admitted|d} literature-signed anomaly signals from {a:adm.n_themes|d} themes with equal theme weights, trades a fraction of the way toward its aim every session, and is costed at $1bn with square-root impact and tiered borrow. The pitched cell is library v7.1 on role lo1: on TRAIN 2020-2022 it earns S2 net Sharpe {summ.net_sharpe|+.3f} (gross {summ.gross_sharpe|.3f}, HAC t {summ.hac_t|.2f}) at all-rows gross leverage {summ.mean_gross_leverage_all_rows|.3f}, daily turnover {summ.tau_gmv_mean|.4f} of GMV, {summ.cost_bps_traded|.2f} bps per traded dollar and a maximum drawdown of {scen.max_drawdown|pct1}.

**How v7 got here.** From the v6.1 baseline ({@v61u-ew-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc-L1.247:summ.net_sharpe|+.3f}) the v7 sprint scored eight TRAIN cells. Three construction variants (C1-C3) and the spo-v1 optimiser were rejected, spo-v1 as an implementation defect. Library v7.0 (wave 1) was accepted at {@v70u-ew-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc-L1.247:summ.net_sharpe|+.3f}; role lo3 (U-lo3) on v7.0 was accepted at {@v70-lo3-ew-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc-L1.247:summ.net_sharpe|+.3f}; the corrected optimiser spo-v2 on that book was rejected as a research result at {@v70-lo3-spo-v2-G1.0:summ.net_sharpe|+.3f}; library v7.1 (wave 2) on lo1 was accepted at {summ.net_sharpe|+.3f}. aim-partial-v5 stays the construction.
**What it is not yet.** Five facts, each with its number, come before any ask.

The linked-operating-v1 restriction then keeps names with exactly one point-in-time issuer link on the primary line, a common share class, and a visible SIC code under 550 days old that is not a pooled vehicle, blank check or royalty trust. It drops {a:univ.dropped_share|pct1} of base member-sessions in the TRAIN window, almost all as unlinked ({a:univ.reason_share.unlinked|pct1}); the kept universe holds {a:univ.kept_min|int} to {a:univ.kept_max|int} names (median {a:univ.kept_median|int}).

Fundamentals (SEC financial statement data) become usable from the first session after the filing's acceptance time plus {a:fields.fund_lag|d} declared lag session; nothing available on or after 2025-01-01 is read. The lowest TRAIN coverage of any field is {a:fields.min_score_cov|pct1}.

paragraphs: **Design.** Library v7.1 holds {a:adm.n|d} candidates in {a:adm.n_themes|d} themes. Each is one canonical variant of a published anomaly, written in a small expression DSL with the literature sign embedded (higher value = long), so no sign is ever estimated from TRAIN. Firm-level accounting ratios are ranked within FF12 industry. Slow signals are smoothed with a 21-session linear decay of the raw value before the rank; the v5.1 fast sleeves (si_change, ind_adj_rev_5, seasonality_same_month, iv_rv_spread) and sv_flow are not smoothed; the v7 members keep their registered forms (DSL table).

**What three years can say about them.** The median admitted candidate has HAC t {a:adm.median_t|.2f}; {a:adm.n_t_gt_2|d} exceed 2 and {a:adm.n_t_gt_1|d} exceed 1, while {a:adm.n_neg_t_admitted|d} admitted members have a negative t ({a:adm.neg_t_admitted}). This is what an un-mined library looks like on 750 days: individually insignificant signals whose blend has a mean daily rank IC of {a:combined.w5.mean|+.4f} at h 5 (Newey-West SE {a:combined.w5.se|.4f}), positive on {a:combined.w5.pos_share|pct0} of days.

**What changed.** v5.1 to v6 replaced weak or mis-specified members with their stronger published forms and moved smoothing in front of the rank; v6.1 added sv_flow. v7.0 (wave 1) added five candidates: q5_eg (HAC t {a:adm.row.q5_eg.hac_t|+.2f}) and smax5 ({a:adm.row.smax5.hac_t|+.2f}) were admitted, qmj_safety was vetoed (t {a:adm.row.qmj_safety.hac_t|+.2f}), nincr was redundant with {a:adm.row.nincr.redundant_with} (|rho| {a:adm.row.nincr.redundant_rho|.2f}) and res_mom_ind with {a:adm.row.res_mom_ind.redundant_with} ({a:adm.row.res_mom_ind.redundant_rho|.2f}). v7.1 (wave 2) added four, all admitted: ins_opp, inst_best_ideas, ftd_fail and ea_overdue, and with them the tenth theme ownership_flow. paragraphs: **Admission v4-prior-v1 estimates neither signs nor weights.** A candidate is rejected only if it has fewer than {a:adm.rules.min_train_days|d} TRAIN days, standalone turnover above {a:adm.rules.tau_limit|.2f}, a HAC t below {a:adm.rules.veto_t|+.1f} (a clear contradiction of its prior), or a factor-return |rho| above {a:adm.rules.rho_limit|.2f} with a member admitted before it in (tier, roster) order, never in TRAIN-Sharpe order. On lo1: {a:adm.n_admitted|d} admitted, {a:adm.n_redundant|d} redundant, {a:adm.n_veto|d} vetoed ({a:adm.veto}).

**Composition ew-theme-v1** gives every theme with an admitted member the same weight, split equally among its members. The reason is statistical: with about 750 days, estimated means are noise, and sample mean-variance needs thousands of months to beat 1/N (DeMiguel, Garlappi and Uppal 2009). The project learned this directly: v3 used TRAIN-estimated signs and mean-variance weights and went from TRAIN SR 1.81 to validation -1.27 (v6-literature.md, lever X). The one challenger, ew-theme-v6 (drop low_risk, merge options into short_interest, shrink fast sleeves), had paired dSR {@v6l-ew6-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc:parent.dsr|+.3f} (SE {@v6l-ew6-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc:parent.se|.3f}) against its parent: the wrong sign, so it was rejected.

**Diversification.** Admitted signals are weakly correlated: mean off-diagonal cross-sectional correlation {a:sig_corr.admitted.mean|+.3f}, within themes {a:theme_corr.sig_corr.within|+.2f}, between themes {a:theme_corr.sig_corr.between|+.2f}. Daily IC series co-move more ({a:ic_corr.admitted.mean|+.3f} off-diagonal), because a factor-rotation day moves many signals at once.

Redundancy is measured on factor returns, not on signals, so two members with correlated signals can both be admitted.
Largest member weight {a:adm.max_w|.4f}: a single-member theme gets the full theme weight.
Negative-t admitted members stay in: dropping them on TRAIN t is exactly the selection the protocol forbids.

paragraphs: **S2, the primary scenario, is a declared, unfitted $1bn cost model.** Every traded dollar pays half-spread {recsc:S2.half_spread_bps|g} bps plus commission {recsc:S2.commission_bps|g} bps, plus square-root impact Y x sigma63 x (|q| / ADV63)^{recsc:S2.impact_delta|g} with Y {recsc:S2.impact_y|g}; fills are capped at {recsc:S2.max_participation|pct0} of 63-day ADV. Financing is a swap (ACT/360): long {recsc:S2.financing.long_spread_bps|g} bps, short {recsc:S2.financing.short_spread_bps|g} bps plus a tier fee of {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.gc|g} (GC), {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.warm|g} (warm) or {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.special|g} bps (special). S1 swaps the trading cost for a flat {recsc:S1.flat_bps|g} bps; S3 writes off names after {recsc:S3.stale_exit_sessions|d} absent session at an adverse haircut.

**Where the money goes** (TRAIN, S2, sums of daily returns): gross {a:costdec.tot.S2.gross_ex_wo|+pct1} of NAV, trading costs {a:costdec.tot.S2.trade|pct1}, financing {a:costdec.fin_share|pct0} of the total drag, net {a:costdec.tot.S2.net|+pct1}. Impact ({a:costdec.tot.S2.imp_bps|.2f} bps per traded $) is {a:costdec.share.impact|pct0} of the drag, the largest component and the one that grows with size.

**Capacity is measured at one point.** Raising L from 1 to 1.247 (+{a:cap.p.V6-U.d_scale_pct|pct0} gross) raised cost per traded $ by {a:cap.p.V6-U.d_cost|.2f} bps, all of it impact; the square-root law predicts {a:cap.p.V6-U.points.1.imp_pred|.2f} bps of impact vs {a:cap.p.V6-U.points.1.imp_bps|.2f} observed. Two points per pair give a local slope; the capacity curve at the end of this section replays the whole book from ${a:capcurve.rows.0.nav_bn|g}bn to ${a:capcurve.max.nav_bn|g}bn.

paragraphs: **Pre-registration.** Every lever set is declared in v4-prereg.md (v7: v7-prereg.md) before any TRAIN read of it, and every result goes into the ledger with a cumulative trial count (Appendix A). A step is accepted if the sign of its paired dSR(net) against its parent matches the declared prior; the size is not a criterion, because over {a:misc.years|.2f} years SE(SR) is about {a:misc.sr_se|.2f} (Lo 2002) and no single lever could clear it.

**Paired statistics.** dSR is the difference of annualised net Sharpe ratios on common sessions. Its Memmel (2003) SE uses the correlation of the two return series (rho {summ.paired.rho|.3f} for the v7.1 step, {a:e2e.rho|.3f} end to end vs v5 REF), which is why the paired SE of a one-lever step is an order of magnitude below an unpaired one. A circular block bootstrap (CBB, block 21, 2000 draws) and the Ledoit-Wolf studentized bootstrap give an interval and a p-value. The deflated Sharpe ratio (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014) is computed against two nulls: cross-cell (SR0 from the variance of the N cells' per-session Sharpe ratios) and Lo (variance (1 + SR^2/2) / T of a single cell).

**Why validation #3 is unspent.** The freeze gate needs a cell-count DSR of at least .95 and the pitched cell has {summ.deflated.dsr|.4f} at N {summ.deflated.n|d}. Every further TRAIN cell raises N, so the pre-registered condition binds; the effective-N figure ({summ.deflated_effective_n.dsr|.4f}) does not replace it. Whether to spend validation #3 anyway, with the shortfall disclosed, is the owner's call (U1).

list: **Timing.** Mark at session d (data known by 22:00 UTC), decide at 23:00 UTC, fill at the close of d+1; the first return row is d+2.

**Desired weights.** Centred tied rank of the combined signal over the session's members, then price-risk-v1: the OLS residual on [1, beta252 vs the equal-weight market, vol63, log ADV63] (clipped z-scores), rescaled to gross 1.

**Aim and partial step.** aim_i = L x desired_i with L {scen.construction.v5.aim_leverage|g}; next_i = cur_i + theta x (aim_i - cur_i) with theta {scen.construction.v5.theta|g}, unless |aim_i - cur_i| is at most dust / N_d (dust {scen.construction.v5.dust_multiple|g}, N_d members), in which case the name does not trade.

**Delta orders.** The order is the planned change in decision-NAV dollars; price drift between decision and fill rides instead of being traded back. The target basis traded back 17-18% of executed dollars as drift (v6-code-review-exec.md F1).

**Exit rate.** A name that leaves the universe decays as cur x (1 - {scen.construction.v5.exit_rate|g}) per session and snaps to 0 inside the dust band, instead of a forced full exit (19-22% of planned turnover at rate 1, review F2).

**Locate-in-aim.** A member in the special borrow tier with a negative desired weight is set to 0 before neutralisation, so the neutraliser sees the book the broker would allow; {sum.locate_in_aim.zeroed_special_short_aims|int} member-decisions were zeroed.

**Missing prints.** A name that stops printing is carried at its last mark with orders blocked and written off after {recsc:S2.stale_exit_sessions|d} absent sessions (S3: {recsc:S3.stale_exit_sessions|d}, with an adverse haircut).

caveats.title: Honest caveats (read before U1)
items: **Freeze gate UNMET.** Cell-count DSR {summ.deflated.dsr|.4f} is below .95 at N {summ.deflated.n|d} (SR0 {summ.deflated.sr0_annual|.3f} annualised). The effective-N DSR, {summ.deflated_effective_n.dsr|.4f} with {summ.deflated_effective_n.n_eff|d} ONC clusters, is shown beside it and never substituted.

**Each accepted step is a sign result at or inside about one SE.** Wave 1 (v7.0 vs v6.1) dSR {j:n34.33.paired.dsr|+.3f} (Memmel SE {j:n34.33.paired.memmel_se|.3f}); U-lo3 (lo3 vs lo1 on v7.0) {j:n35.34.paired.dsr|+.3f} (SE {j:n35.34.paired.memmel_se|.3f}); wave 2 (v7.1 vs v7.0) {summ.paired.dsr|+.3f} (SE {summ.paired.memmel_se|.3f}, t {summ.paired.t|.2f}; CBB 95% [{summ.paired.cbb_ci95|+.3f}]).

**Wave 2 reads as diversification, not as four new signals.** Standalone TRAIN HAC t: ins_opp {a:adm.row.ins_opp.hac_t|+.2f}, inst_best_ideas {a:adm.row.inst_best_ideas.hac_t|+.2f}, ftd_fail {a:adm.row.ftd_fail.hac_t|+.2f}, ea_overdue {a:adm.row.ea_overdue.hac_t|+.2f}; none above 1 in absolute value. ins_opp's TRAIN IC sign ({a:adm.row.ins_opp.runner_sign|+.0f}) is against its prior ({a:adm.row.ins_opp.prior_sign|+.0f}); the rule orients by the prior and vetoes only below t -2, so it is admitted with the prior sign and currently subtracts. The gain is best read as diversification from a tenth theme (ownership_flow; {a:adm.n_themes|d} themes at 1/{a:adm.n_themes|d} each) diluting the other nine.

**Correction.** The earlier handoff quoted the v6.1 baseline at "N 33"; its figure was the N {j:n32.28.deflated.n|d} value ({j:n32.28.deflated.dsr|.4f}). With the defective spo-v1 cell inside the cross-cell variance the baseline scores {j:n33.28.deflated.dsr|.4f} at N {j:n33.28.deflated.n|d} (ruling 7.0-e: the variance stays "all ledgered cells"; whether defect cells belong in it is an owner question).

**TRAIN only.** {a:misc.years|.2f} years, 2020-2022. The 2023-2024 window was read twice at book level (validation trials #1, v3, and #2, v4.1) and never in v6, v6.1 or v7; a third read (#3) needs the owner (U1). 2025 onward is reserved.

**V7-F is pre-registered, both of its conditions are met, and it has NOT been run.** V7-F is library v7.1 on role lo3: it was declared to run only if both v7.1 (wave 2, on lo1) and U-lo3 (lo3, on v7.0) were accepted, and both were. The owner asked to stop at the next logical point, and V7-F needs the fields-v9 stage on lo3, whose cycle plumbing was stopped at design. Their combination is untested; it would be cell N 38.

**2020 contributes little.** 2020 is {a:misc.first_year_share|pct0} of the summed yearly returns; the universe restriction lifted 2021-2022 and removed most of the 2020 alpha that the unrestricted role had (the unrestricted loc cell made {@v6l-ew-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc:scen.calendar_year_returns.0.net_compounded_return|+pct1} in 2020).

**Costs are declared, not fitted.** Measured on V6-U, cost per traded $ rises from {a:cap.p.V6-U.points.0.cost_bps|.2f} to {a:cap.p.V6-U.points.1.cost_bps|.2f} bps between L 1 and L 1.247: impact is convex, so more AUM or more gross loses more.

**Borrow is predicted, not quoted.** Tiers come from public characteristics (market cap, price, short-interest ratio, IPO age). Special-tier short aims are zeroed ({sum.locate_in_aim.zeroed_special_short_aims|int} member-decisions); hard-to-borrow cost may still be understated.
**Identity.** The universe restriction, the largest v6 step, rests on a rehearsal identity bridge (scope_complete {a:univ.scope_complete}).

survivorship.title: Survivorship and look-ahead
items: Membership is point in time (as-of member mask, one-session lag), so names that later delisted are in the panel while they traded.

Delisting returns are not modelled. A name that stops printing is written off at its last mark after {recsc:S2.stale_exit_sessions|d} absent sessions in S2; S3 writes it off after {recsc:S3.stale_exit_sessions|d} session with haircuts long {recsc:S3.terminal_haircut_long|+pct0} / short {recsc:S3.terminal_haircut_short|+pct0} and is the stress for this gap (S3 net {scen:S3.net_sharpe|+.3f}).
The membership recipe keeps the ADV top-N rule as an upper envelope; the linked-operating restriction is applied on top of it.
Nothing available on or after 2025-01-01 is read (the seal is asserted in the fields manifest).

cost_gaps.title: What the cost model does not include
items: Name-level borrow fees and recalls: tiers are predicted (market cap below $1bn, price below $5, SI ratio at least .10, IPO age under one year), not quoted. engine-tiers ({recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.special|g} bps special, {recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.warm|g} bps warm) is the stress.
Short-sale constraints beyond the special-tier block: no locate failures, no recalls, no short-sale price test.
Closing-auction realism: fills at the close at a modelled cost, with no auction-imbalance or queue model beyond the {recsc:S2.max_participation|pct0} ADV cap.
A constant spread for every name, and an impact coefficient that is declared, not fitted to fills.
No rebate on short proceeds and no interest on cash (excess-return accounting).

one_se.title: What "one SE" means for a three-year window
paragraphs: With T = {a:misc.years|.2f} years, the Lo SE of an annualised Sharpe near {summ.net_sharpe|.2f} is {a:misc.sr_se|.2f}, so its 95% interval runs from {a:misc.sr_ci_lo|+.2f} to {a:misc.sr_ci_hi|+.2f}. Separating nearby Sharpe ratios without pairing would take decades. Pairing near-identical books is far tighter (Memmel SE {summ.paired.memmel_se|.3f} for the v7.1 step), yet no accepted step cleared about one SE: the evidence for any single lever is its literature prior, not TRAIN.

`linear-6bps-stale5-v1+swap-fin-v1`: a flat {recsc:S1.flat_bps|g} bps per traded dollar, no impact, no participation cap; same financing as S2.

`modeled-1bn-terminal-adverse-v1+swap-fin-v1`: S2 costs, but a name is written off after {recsc:S3.stale_exit_sessions|d} absent session with haircut long {recsc:S3.terminal_haircut_long|+pct0} / short {recsc:S3.terminal_haircut_short|+pct0}; the delisting stress.
S2 trading costs with financing `flat-300-v0`: a flat {recsc:flat300.financing.flat_short_bps|g} bps a year on shorts (ACT/365), no long spread, special shorts not blocked.

S2 trading costs with financing `engine-tiers-v1`: tier fees GC {recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.gc|g}, warm {recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.warm|g}, special {recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.special|g} bps a year.

Swap financing, ACT/360: long {recsc:S2.financing.long_spread_bps|g} bps, short {recsc:S2.financing.short_spread_bps|g} bps plus a tier fee of {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.gc|g} / {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.warm|g} / {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.special|g} bps. The tier is predicted per name per decision from public flags (market cap below $1bn, price below $5, SI ratio at least .10, IPO age under 365 days): 0 flags GC, 1 warm, 2 or more special. Special shorts are blocked.
Trading cost dollars (spread + commission + impact) per traded dollar of fills, in basis points.
Annualised Sharpe ratio (x sqrt 252) of daily NAV returns after / before trading costs and financing; excess-return accounting (no cash interest).
t statistic of the mean daily net return with a Newey-West (Bartlett kernel) long-run variance.

Daily one-way turnover in GMV units: sum of |filled dollars| / pre-trade gross, executed fills only, deployment session excluded. Candidate tau (admission) is the same on a candidate's standalone factor.
(long$ + short$) / NAV and (long$ - short$) / NAV averaged over every daily CSV row, including the deployment ramp; the R6' gate basis.
The same means over rows after the first 63 sessions, once the partial-step book has deployed; the basis for calibrating L.
Names held / members; above 1 when exited nonmembers are still decaying out.
Maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of the net NAV.
The construction rule: each session every member moves next = cur + theta x (L x desired - cur), unless inside the dust band (section 5).
Aim leverage, the multiplier on the gross-1 desired book; final cell {scen.construction.v5.aim_leverage|g}.
Trade fraction: the share of the gap between aim and current closed per session ({scen.construction.v5.theta|g}; half-life about {a:misc.half_life|.0f} sessions).
No-trade band multiple: a name trades only if |aim - cur| exceeds dust / N_d ({scen.construction.v5.dust_multiple|g}).
Per-session decay rate of a nonmember's position ({scen.construction.v5.exit_rate|g}); rate 1 is the immediate exit.
Delta: the order is the planned dollar change at decision NAV, so drift rides. Target: the order re-targets the planned weight at fill, trading drift back.
Special-tier short aims set to 0 before neutralisation (v6 prereg C3).

Neutraliser: OLS residual of the tied-rank target on [1, beta252 vs the equal-weight market, vol63, log ADV63], rescaled to the entry gross. price-risk-ind-v1 / v2 add FF12 demeaning (v2 with vol126 / ADV252); both rejected.
The first ~63 sessions, when the book deploys from zero at rate theta.
Information coefficient: the cross-sectional (rank) correlation of a signal at decision d with the forward return close[d+1+h] / close[d+1] - 1; h in sessions (5, 21, 63).
The expression language the alphas are written in (rank, group_rank, decay_linear, delay, ts_sum, correlation, group_neutralize, ...).
Rank of the 21-session linear-decayed raw value vs the decayed rank; v6 moved smoothing before the rank for slow signals and removed it for fast sleeves.
The literature direction; embedded in the DSL (a -1 multiplier where the raw direction is -1), so every candidate's prior sign is +1.
Literature evidence grade A+ to D (replication, post-publication decay, large-cap evidence); orders the redundancy screen.
The composition unit: value, profitability_quality, investment_issuance, earnings_momentum, price_momentum, low_risk, short_interest, reversal_seasonality, options_implied.
A candidate with standalone tau at or above .08.

Admission screen: prior signs, reject on too few days, turnover above {a:adm.rules.tau_limit|.2f}, HAC t below {a:adm.rules.veto_t|+.1f} or |rho| above {a:adm.rules.rho_limit|.2f}; no sign or weight estimation.

Composition: equal weight per theme with an admitted member, equal within theme. ew-theme-v6 (rejected) dropped low_risk, merged options into short_interest and shrank fast sleeves; ew-theme-aim-v1 (v5) weighted by aim gain.
Paired difference of annualised net Sharpe ratios of two cells on common return sessions (S2).
Standard error of dSR under the Jobson-Korkie test with the Memmel (2003) correction; uses the return correlation rho of the two cells.
Circular block bootstrap of dSR: blocks of 21 sessions, 2000 draws, 95% percentile interval.
Ledoit-Wolf (2008) studentized circular block bootstrap test of equal Sharpe ratios; reported as a p-value.

Deflated Sharpe ratio (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014): the probability that the true SR exceeds SR0, the expected maximum of N null Sharpe ratios. Cross-cell takes the variance of SR from the N cells; Lo takes (1 + SR^2/2) / T for the cell alone.
N: number of NAV cells counted as trials ({summ.deflated.n|d}); SR0: the deflation benchmark; T: return sessions ({summ.return_rows|d}).
Newey-West SE of a mean daily IC series with lag 2h (overlapping forward returns).

A role is the pinned research panel (sessions x instruments, member mask, prices). Role v2 is the top-3000-by-ADV TRAIN role; lo1 is role v2 restricted by linked-operating-v1. lo3 is the v2 rule with the SIC table of the atx-db fundamentals stage (linked-operating-v3), accepted as a universe trial on library v7.0.
Universe restriction: one PIT issuer link on the primary line, common class, visible SIC under 550 days old, not a pooled vehicle, blank check or royalty trust (SIC {a:univ.non_operating_sic}).
The lo1 field set: the {a:fields.n_fields|d} research fields (fields-v6b plus sv_ratio126), each with a clock, staleness rule and coverage.
Point in time: a cell's value and whether it is missing use only information available by the decision (22:00 UTC mark, 23:00 UTC decision).
Fama-French 12 / 49 industry groups from the SIC code; used for within-industry ranks and demeaning.
The dated CIK-to-security link table (r4 rehearsal, scope_complete false) that joins filings to listings.
TRAIN = 2020-2022 (all selection and estimation). VAL = 2023-2024, three book-level validation trials in total, two spent. Holdout = 2025 onward, reserved and never read.
Any run whose statistic could influence a choice: each admission candidate, composition, universe and NAV cell. Reproductions with identical bytes are not trials.
The cumulative trial-accounting block every TRAIN result carries in the ledger.
The mechanics gate: all-rows gross in [.90, 1.05], |mean net| at most .02, tau mean at most .20 and p95 at most .30.

paragraphs: **How much capital the book takes.** The capacity pass replays the final book at ${a:capcurve.rows.0.nav_bn|g}bn to ${a:capcurve.max.nav_bn|g}bn: the square-root impact is scaled to each NAV and the 1%-of-ADV participation cap binds on the larger book. Net Sharpe falls from {a:capcurve.x1.net_sharpe|+.3f} at ${a:capcurve.base_nav_bn|g}bn to {a:capcurve.max.net_sharpe|+.3f} at ${a:capcurve.max.nav_bn|g}bn ({a:capcurve.sr_retained_max|pct0} retained), and cost per traded dollar rises from {a:capcurve.x1.cost_bps_per_traded_dollar|.2f} to {a:capcurve.max.cost_bps_per_traded_dollar|.2f} bps. Against a net-SR threshold of {a:capcurve.threshold|g} the curve is {a:capcurve.cross_how} (the crossing is interpolated in log NAV when there is one). At the top of the grid {a:capcurve.max.capped_share|pct1} of fills hit the cap, so fills are rationed as well as priced higher.

**Impact-law risk.** The same $1bn book priced with the Kyle-Obizhaeva invariance law (S2-KO) or the Frazzini-Israel-Moskowitz fit (S2-FIM) instead of the square-root law nets {a:capcurve.book.S2-KO.net_sharpe|+.3f} and {a:capcurve.book.S2-FIM.net_sharpe|+.3f}, against {a:capcurve.book.S2.net_sharpe|+.3f} under S2. S2 stays the primary scenario as pre-registered; the alternatives are reported, not chosen.

blocks.text: Integrity statistics after the v7 trials

paragraphs: **How honest the statistics are.** The pitched cell is scored at N {a:integrity.final.n|d}, every scored TRAIN construction cell in the ledger. Its cell-count DSR is {a:integrity.final.dsr|.4f} (SR0 {a:integrity.final.sr0|.3f}): the freeze gate asks for .95 and is UNMET. Against the effective number of independent trials ({a:integrity.final.n_eff|d} ONC clusters of {a:integrity.final.n_trials|d}) it is {a:integrity.final.dsr_eff|.4f}; that figure is reported beside the gate statistic and never replaces it. The table shows how the same cells moved as N grew: the v6.1 baseline scored {j:n32.28.deflated.dsr|.4f} at N {j:n32.28.deflated.n|d} and {j:n33.28.deflated.dsr|.4f} at N {j:n33.28.deflated.n|d}, once the defective spo-v1 cell (S2 net {@v61u-spo-v1-L1.247:summ.net_sharpe|+.3f}) entered the cross-cell variance; the earlier handoff's "N 33" figure for the baseline was the N {j:n32.28.deflated.n|d} value. The protocol's variance is all ledgered cells (ruling 7.0-e); whether defect cells belong in it is an owner question. PSR(0) is {a:integrity.final.psr0|.4f}, and rejecting SR 0 at 95% needs a track record of {a:integrity.final.mintrl0_y|.1f} years ({a:integrity.final.mintrl0_s|int} sessions). CSCV PBO over all {a:integrity.pbo.-1.n|d} cells is {a:integrity.pbo.-1.pbo|.3f}, against a pre-registered limit of {a:integrity.pbo_max|g}.

Every scored TRAIN construction cell is a line in the append-only ledger, identified by the SHA-256 of its daily return series, so a re-run adds no trial. The ledger's N is the N of the cell-count DSR. Admission and composition trials are counted in Appendix A; they are not in this N. Every line carries its verdict from the cell table: the v7 lines are C1-C3 and spo-v2 rejected, spo-v1 rejected as a defect, v7.0, U-lo3 and v7.1 accepted. Validation: 2 of 3 trials spent (2023-2024, book level, #1 v3 and #2 v4.1); 2025 onward reserved.

layout.title: Risks, open items and path to production

paragraphs: **Is the risk forecast honest?** A risk model is unbiased when realised returns divided by the forecast volatility have a standard deviation of 1 (the bias statistic b); b below 1 means realised risk came in under the forecast. Under {j:risk11.model} over 252-session windows b averages {a:bias.fam.factor.b252|.3f} for the factor-mimicking portfolios and {a:bias.fam.random.b252|.3f} for random dollar-neutral portfolios. {a:bias.structural_factors|d} short-history factors are forecast structurally, and {a:bias.dropped_total|d} observations were dropped for an unforecast exposure.

**Why v1.1: atx-risk-v1 was corrupt at the source.** The R2 review of spo-v2 (ledger, 2026-09-29) found that one asset_growth outlier collapsed that style into a one-name dummy on 259 dates; the resulting structural specific variance reached 3.9e12 and decile shrinkage spread it to 176 names (the F2 pin's maximum daily specific variance was 9.0e12). v1.1 fences every descriptor at a robust MAD bound, does not regress a style below {j:risk11.robustness.style_floor_effective_names|g} effective names, and refuses any specific variance outside (0, {j:risk11.robustness.specific_variance_bound|g}) instead of clamping it: the largest daily specific variance is now {j:risk11.robustness.max_daily_specific_variance.value|.3f}, with {j:risk11.robustness.invariant_refusals|d} refusals and {j:risk11.robustness.style_dates_dropped|d} style-dates dropped. The risk model is descriptive in v7: it is not an input of the pitched book, and spo-v2, the one construction that used it, was rejected.

layout.title: Running the book: decisions, orders, reconciliation, monitoring

paragraphs: **From model to orders (measured on the v6.1 book).** The loop below was built and measured in task W4 on the v6.1 book (the v7-w4-* runs); the v7.1 book uses the same code and has not been replayed through it. Each day the replay's own code turns the actual positions into target weights (`decide`), then into lot-rounded share orders for a market-on-close fill; the next day's broker positions are reconciled against the expected holdings. At {a:ops.n_decisions_read|d} TRAIN as-of dates the decided targets equal the replay's bit for bit ({a:ops.parity_total|d} mismatches), at most {a:ops.wall_max|.1f} s per decision. Reconciliation finds {a:ops.self_breaks|d} breaks when the broker file is the expected one, and {a:ops.expect_met|d} of {a:ops.expect_n|d} reconcile runs give exactly the expected counts, the planted breaks included. Emitting the holdings costs {a:ops.wall_ratio|.2f}x the NAV wall time.
check: All as-of dates are TRAIN dates; no live data or broker has touched the loop yet.
Health warnings (no locate file, stale names, data freshness under --allow-stale) are expected on a historical replay and are named per decision.

paragraphs: The daily book monitor replayed over TRAIN puts {a:monitor_base.sleeve_counts.alarm|d} sleeve(s) in alarm ({a:monitor_base.alarming_names}), {a:monitor_base.sleeve_counts.warn|d} on warn and {a:monitor_base.sleeve_counts.ok|d} at ok. It raises flags only; retiring or reweighting a sleeve stays an owner decision. M1, the bias test of the book itself, reads {a:monitor_base.checks.M1.status}: it needs a risk run that includes the book's holdings. Because the baseline sets its thresholds on the same TRAIN window it is checked on, this is a calibration, not a test; the first live read is the test.
